capability_matrix.notes: The observed Codex pair uses initialize plus session state; the final next protocol removes the handshake and protocol session.
The isolated Python MCP 2.0.0 KAG adapter served server/discover; Codex 0.146.0 was still observed sending initialize instead.

The isolated read-only KAG requestState handle passed bearer principal isolation, expiry, cross-request replay denial, tamper denial, and key-retirement revocation; same-request replay is allowed only for the idempotent read pilot.
The isolated KAG adapter proved self-describing requests across two clients with no session header or server-request backchannel; explicit application handles remain unproved.
The isolated KAG adapter preserved traceparent at pair level; trace metadata remains observation only and never becomes owner authority.

The isolated KAG pair proved private TTL hits, exact-expiry refetch, subscription addition invalidation, removal revocation, no-listener staleness, explicit refresh, and that stale discovery cannot authorize a removed tool.
Tasks is a separate extension and cannot be inferred from core support; Python MCP 2.0.0 explicitly does not implement the 2026-07-28 Tasks extension.
Next marks the legacy core features deprecated; removal is not implied.
Next widens tool schemas and output values; depth, external refs, and validator budgets need pair tests.

claim_limits: Protocol literals in a binary do not prove negotiated wire support.
A stable SDK release does not prove Codex pair support.
Official conformance does not prove Abyss owner, freshness, effect, or rollback behavior.
A read canary does not admit candidate or effect organs.
A registered alias does not prove schema observation or a grounded call.
Final publication and stable SDKs never authorize production migration without exact pair receipts.

migration_gates.requirement: Run official conformance against the exact pair.

migration_gates.reason: The isolated KAG pair passed discovery, stateless, auth, limits and read behavior, but client cancellation did not stop the server dispatch; exact pair-conformance remains blocked on propagation.
The source-authored stable/next capability comparison is present and validated.
The isolated KAG pair used two independent clients with self-describing requests, no protocol session header, and no server-request backchannel.

The isolated read-only KAG pair proved opaque requestState round trips, bearer principal isolation, expiry, cross-request replay denial, tamper denial, and key-retirement revocation; same-request replay remained safe and idempotent.
The isolated Python MCP 2.0.0 KAG adapter served server/discover at 2026-07-28; Codex consumer support remains independently blocked by P1-03.
The isolated KAG pair preserved trace context and proved private TTL hits, exact-expiry refetch, subscription invalidation, removal revocation, bounded stale-catalog behavior, and explicit refresh.
Python MCP 2.0.0 documents the 2026-07-28 Tasks extension but does not implement it; no exact Abyss Tasks pair can be formed on this SDK line.
The stable registration is retained and the disabled next lab name is non-replacing.
The separately named and credentialed aoa_kag_next_lab registration performed one exact kag_discover call through Codex 0.147.0-alpha.4 on MCP 2026-07-28.

The isolated process, endpoint, credential, registration and CODEX_HOME were removed; the operator config remained byte-identical and the production aoa_kag registration passed a real post-rollback canary.

rollback: Stop and remove only the next lab registration.
Verify the stable aoa_kag registration was never changed.
Re-run the stable read canary and compare its schema digest.

refresh_triggers: The final 2026-07-28 specification tag or exact commit changes.
Python or TypeScript v2 publishes a new stable release.
Codex changes version or documents next-era client support.
The official conformance suite changes version or scenarios.
Any server SDK pin, schema, transport, auth, or registration changes.
